entries.clue: Film director's family felt the heat at first (8)

indicatorNotes.at first: tells you FRIED comes first, ahead of KIN

blocks.note: fried = felt the heat, as food in a pan

annotation.surface: A director's relatives wilt under pressure, or in a heatwave.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is written back to front: 'family' is read first but goes second. William Friedkin directed The Exorcist and The French Connection.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Friedkin, who made The Exorcist and The French Connection, is one film director, named only by his job.

entries.clue: Poorly insured son is going bankrupt (6)

indicatorNotes.Poorly: the letters are in bad shape, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: An ill man learns his insurance won't stop the family business going under.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is going' reads like part of 'going bankrupt' but it belongs with 'son': S departs. 'Bankrupt' as an adjective matches RUINED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the financial sense: a ruined firm has lost everything, which is what bankrupt means.

entries.clue: New exotic pen in special case (9)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made new, into a fresh order

annotation.surface: A fancy new fountain pen sits in its presentation box.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like the box the pen comes in; it is part of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrase names something the usual rule does not apply to.

entries.clue: They swim off across river (5)

indicatorNotes.across: KILL stretches across R, holding it

blocks.note: to off someone is to kill them

annotation.surface: Swimmers push away from the bank and head across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as swimming away; it is the slang verb for murder. The definition is a bare description: krill swim.
annotation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny crustaceans that swim in vast ocean swarms.

entries.clue: Most impressive split headline is French (7)

indicatorNotes.split: tells you to break 'headline' into head + line

blocks.note: split into head (NOB, slang for head) and line (L)

annotation.surface: A newspaper splits a headline in two and prints it in French.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Headline' looks like one word of journalism but is two: NOB for head, L for line. 'Nob' is old British slang for the head.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: noble means grand or stately, and the superlative ending matches 'Most'.

entries.clue: Nutcases operated in Langley? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' as a place word: RAN is to be found in CIA, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the CIA's headquarters is at Langley, Virginia

annotation.surface: Madmen were running things at CIA headquarters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nutcases' reads as lunatics; split it as nut-cases, and a skull is the case for the head, slang 'nut'.
annotation.definitionFit: Crania, skulls, are the cases that hold the 'nut', or head.

entries.clue: Italian composer has a revolutionary massage in India (9)

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the crossword's stock revolutionary
I = India in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An Italian composer on tour treats himself to a rebel-style massage in India.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In India' looks like a location but gives two pieces, IN and I.
annotation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and church music.

entries.clue: Everyone around the Bluegrass state is radical (5)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' as encircling: ALL wraps round KY on both sides

blocks.note: KY = Kentucky, nicknamed the Bluegrass State

annotation.surface: Everybody in Kentucky has extreme politics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical' is political on the surface but chemical in the answer: an alkyl is a radical, a group of atoms, such as methyl.
annotation.definitionFit: In chemistry an alkyl group, such as methyl, is called a radical.

entries.clue: Dinner set occasionally given to act as compensation (2,6)

indicatorNotes.occasionally: take only some letters, every other one
indicatorNotes.given to: INRE is handed to TURN, so the two join

blocks.note: a turn = an act on a variety bill

annotation.surface: A dinner service is handed over now and then to pay someone back.
annotation.walkthrough: The alternate letters stop at E; the final T of 'set' is left out. 'Turn' is a stage act, as in a comedian doing a turn.
annotation.definitionFit: Something given in return is given as compensation.

entries.clue: Wave after round trip (7,7)

blocks.note: a circuit = a round, as of a track
a breaker is a large wave

annotation.surface: A wave of illness follows a return journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round trip' is a false phrase: 'round' is wordplay and 'trip' alone is the definition. A circuit breaker is the switch that trips when a circuit overloads.
annotation.definitionFit: A circuit breaker is also called a trip switch, since it trips to cut the power.

entries.clue: Writer attached to China as correspondent (3,3)

indicatorNotes.attached to: 'attached to' as fastened on: PAL is fixed onto the end of PEN

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, the thing you write with
rhyming slang: china plate = mate, so china = pal

annotation.surface: A writer is posted to China as a foreign correspondent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to look like the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' for mate.
annotation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone you correspond with by letter.

entries.clue: English characteristic that the elitists might not like? (8)

annotation.definition: that the elitists might not like?
annotation.surface: A national trait that snobs would disapprove of.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description rather than a synonym, hence the question mark: elitists prefer hierarchy to equality.
annotation.definitionFit: Elitists believe some people are better than others, so equality is what they would dislike.

entries.clue: Some fritter billions, 8 for Da Ponte's works? (8)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the words
indicatorNotes.8 for: 8 down is IN RETURN, so the letters come back the other way

annotation.surface: Someone squanders billions in exchange for Da Ponte's operas.
annotation.walkthrough: '8 for' borrows the answer to 8 down, IN RETURN, as a reversal signal. Lorenzo Da Ponte wrote the words for Mozart's Figaro, Don Giovanni and Così.
annotation.definitionFit: Da Ponte was a librettist, so his works are libretti, the texts of operas.

entries.clue: People who sell Dior's latest and earliest fashions (9)

indicatorNotes.fashions: as a verb: shapes the letters into something new

annotation.surface: Shops that sell both the newest and the earliest Dior collections.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a noun in a Dior clue; it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: shopkeepers selling goods to the public rather than to the trade.

entries.clue: Unelected Head of State visits a European port (4)

indicatorNotes.visits: to visit is to go into someone's place, so CR goes inside A E

blocks.note: CR = Carolus Rex, King Charles's royal cipher

annotation.surface: A king makes a state visit to a European harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A European port' reads as one phrase, but Acre is in Israel: 'port' alone is the definition. CR is King Charles's cipher, as ER was the Queen's.
annotation.definitionFit: Acre is an ancient port on the coast of northern Israel.

entries.clue: American carved a large breast in white stone (9)

indicatorNotes.carved: the letters are cut into a new shape

annotation.surface: An American sculptor carves a big bust out of white marble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carved' fits the stone so well it passes for description; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft, fine-grained white stone used for carving.

entries.clue: Jack the Ripper copycat taking pee? He sprays all over the place (8)

annotation.definition: He sprays all over the place

indicatorNotes.taking: 'taking' as taking in, absorbing: SLASHER takes P into its middle

blocks.note: a slasher is a knife-wielding attacker
the letter P, as it sounds

annotation.surface: A copycat killer turns out to be merely someone urinating everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pee' is the spoken name of the letter P, not a bodily function, though the surface wants it to be both.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful coinage: the -ER ending makes a person out of the verb splash, and the definition describes that messy habit.

entries.clue: Start working after drinking a short (4)

indicatorNotes.drinking: a drinker takes liquid inside, so ON takes PE inside it
indicatorNotes.short: PER is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: a = per (as in 'twice a day'), cut short to PE

annotation.surface: Someone starts the working day after knocking back a short, a small strong drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A short' looks like a whisky; 'a' means per, as in fifty miles an hour, and 'short' clips it to PE. 'After' only joins.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you open a meeting or a debate when you begin it.

entries.clue: Island king into heavy metal and current pop (8)

indicatorNotes.into: 'into' as entering: R goes into TIN, landing in its middle

annotation.surface: An island king gets into heavy metal and modern pop music.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all music, heavy metal and current pop, but each word is chemistry, physics or family.
annotation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

entries.clue: Loosely, it means 10s? (7)

indicatorNotes.Loosely: the letters are taken loosely, not in order

annotation.surface: A dictionary shrugs that the word roughly means tens.
annotation.walkthrough: 10 across is PEN PAL, so '10s' are pen pals: read cryptically, mates in the pen (prison), which is what inmates are.
annotation.definitionFit: Inmates are prison pals, mates in the pen, a jokey reading of pen pals.

entries.clue: Doctor's striking costume (3-3)

blocks.note: to doctor = to rig, tamper with

annotation.surface: A doctor wears an eye-catching outfit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb and 'striking' means on strike, not eye-catching. 'Rig-out' is British for an outfit.
annotation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a complete outfit, which makes costume a close synonym.

entries.clue: Circulated document provided one better political stance (8)

indicatorNotes.Circulated: sent round, so the whole string turns back

annotation.surface: A memo is sent round proposing a better political line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circulated' reads as sending a memo round the office; it reverses everything after it. 'Better' is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: opposing all war is one political position a person may take.

entries.clue: Home Office supports regular uprising (5)

indicatorNotes.supports: in a down answer LOO sits beneath, holding IG up
indicatorNotes.uprising: GI rises, reading upwards as IG

blocks.note: a GI is a regular soldier
'the offices' is an old euphemism for the lavatory

annotation.surface: The Home Office backs a routine rebellion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Home Office' is the British interior ministry, but the words split: 'Home' is the definition and 'Office' the toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: An igloo is a home built of snow blocks.

entries.clue: One rarely scores work at the start of a romance (6)

indicatorNotes.at the start of: GO is placed in front of A LIE

blocks.note: to romance is to invent stories, so a romance is a lie

annotation.surface: A lothario rarely succeeds when he's working at the beginning of an affair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scores' is sexual in the surface but footballing in the definition: goalkeepers seldom score goals.
annotation.definitionFit: A goalie is a goalkeeper, a player who rarely scores.

entries.clue: Despair for one pair of soldiers (5)

indicatorNotes.pair of: a pair is two, so two different soldiers follow one another

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
a soldier ant, one of the colony's defenders

annotation.surface: Someone gives up hope over a couple of soldiers.
annotation.walkthrough: Giant Despair is the giant of Doubting Castle in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, so Despair is one example of a giant. 'Pair of soldiers' means two different soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Despair is the ogre who imprisons Christian in Doubting Castle.

entries.clue: Author in Hanoi's Premier Hotel worked out pi (6-4-4)

indicatorNotes.worked out: the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: A writer at a Hanoi hotel calculates pi.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pi' sits at the end looking like maths; it is the crossword abbreviation for pious.
annotation.definitionFit: Pi, short for pious, describes someone sanctimonious, holier-than-thou.

entries.clue: Bears seen in British castles (6)

blocks.note: in chess the castle is the rook

annotation.surface: Bears have been spotted living in British castles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bears' is a verb, to tolerate; the animals are a decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: To brook is to bear or tolerate, as in 'brooks no argument'.

entries.clue: Planet virtually consumed in swamp (8)

indicatorNotes.virtually: almost all of it: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A whole planet has been swallowed by a marsh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swamp' reads as a bog but it is a verb, to flood or drench.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to flood or drench something, soaking it completely.
